outlier.evidence: All four reviewers rated 6 (h23K, 6Pv4, yA7o, rBKj) at confidence 3, 3, 3 and 2. No score stands apart. Reviewer_h23K's text ('the contributions on the theory side are not major') reads lower than its 6.

inattentive_reviews.evidence: 2 hours spent; 'I did not check the proofs'; asks for experiments on an identification-theory paper; its 2021-09-10 update ('I still think the authors should take these concerns more seriously') names no specific gap in the rebuttal.

checkable_claims.claim: Theorem 2 needs a surrogate set that 'converts the problem to the original one' (the MGT setting).
checkable_claims.evidence: Section 4 and Fig. 5b: the generalized criterion runs the MGT loop with a surrogate experiment Q_s'(W) = Q(W|U,s')Q(U) in place of P(W) = P(W|U)P(U). The added generality is sets, an interventional base distribution and the Z' subset. That this is shallow is opinion. The rebuttal did not answer the point.

checkable_claims.claim: The results are 'only one-way theorems' (sufficient conditions).
checkable_claims.evidence: Theorems 1 and 2 state 'identifiable if'; Theorem 4 states only that ID-ME is sound. The authors concede that completeness is open (replies to Reviewer_rBKj and Reviewer_9UEy).

checkable_claims.claim: P_{a,B}(C,d) should be a |X_C| x |X_B| matrix, not |X_B| x |X_C| (line 114).
checkable_claims.evidence: Authors: 'You are right, thanks for catching the typo.' The PDF in the folder is the camera-ready and reads |X_C| x |X_B| (Section 3).

checkable_claims.claim: Lines 56-57 call P_x(y) in Fig. 1d not identifiable by either approach without saying why.
checkable_claims.evidence: The authors concede that 'not identified' is the right term (a hedge after projecting out U1). The camera-ready reads 'the effect is not identified from each approach'.

checkable_claims.claim: The paper shows that existing sound identification procedures are not complete.
checkable_claims.evidence: Proposition 1: on X->A->B->Y with P(X,B), P(A,B), P(A,Y), P_x(y) = P(y|A)P(B|A)^+P(B|x) (pseudoinverse). The algebra holds: P(y|A) = P(y|B)P(B|A), P(B|x) = P(B|A)P(A|x), and M M^+ M = M.

rebuttal.evidence: Reviewer_h23K's only edit is on its posting day (2021-07-15). Reviewer_6Pv4 and Reviewer_rBKj never edited. Reviewer_yA7o edited on 2021-09-10 and added an update that keeps its concerns and reports no score change. No A reviewer replied to the authors in the forum.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: The authors answered Reviewer_h23K's depth critique with general claims ('Algorithm 1 (ID-ME) is the most general identification algorithm known to date'), not with a reply on Theorem 2. They put experiments and the continuous case off as future work, which Reviewer_yA7o did not accept. They promised presentation fixes for the extra page. The meta-review reports private discussion in which reviewers 'saw merit', but no score rose.

ac.evidence: Two-sentence meta-review: 'The paper was very difficult to follow, but after a fair bit of discussion, reviewers saw merit in the results presented, despite the difficulty with presentation.' Four 6s became a poster. The AC's framing ('(everywhere) identification ... (generic) identification') shows field expertise, but the AC made no case for a higher tier.

main_reasons_for_decision: Four uniform 6s ('marginally above the acceptance threshold') at confidence 2 to 3, with no champion
Paper judged 'very difficult to follow' (meta-review); readability capped enthusiasm
Doubt about depth: Theorem 2 seen as a reduction to MGT (Reviewer_h23K); seen as journal material with proofs unchecked (Reviewer_6Pv4)

outlier.evidence: Ratings 8 (9UEy), 6 (iUkv, up from 5) and 7 (kvzq) lie within two points. Reviewer_9UEy holds the top score but is not an outlier.

checkable_claims.claim: Miao et al. need a rank condition on the proxies; this paper may need none.
checkable_claims.evidence: Theorem 1 requires full column rank of Q(W|U,x); Theorem 2 requires invertible Q(W|U,s') and Q(U|z/(S u Z'),x); (C4) restates the MGT rank |X_U|. The authors replied the same way. kvzq's wider point, that the assumptions are 'strewn throughout', is fair: they sit inside long theorem statements.

checkable_claims.claim: Line 164 (Lemma 2) should have no sum over z.
checkable_claims.evidence: The sum over z is the marginalization over Z, a subset of both X_i and Y_j, that Lemma 2 writes as a matrix product (Section 3, text before Lemma 2). The camera-ready keeps it, and the authors replied that the line is correct.

checkable_claims.claim: The algorithm identifies effects that earlier algorithms cannot, so those algorithms are incomplete.
checkable_claims.evidence: Proposition 1 (pseudoinverse on X->A->B->Y); Theorem 5 claims strict subsumption of the proxy criteria, GID(-PO), mID and eID.

checkable_claims.claim: ID-ME is proven sound but not complete.
checkable_claims.evidence: Theorem 4 ('ID-ME is sound'); there is no completeness result. The authors call completeness their main open question.

rebuttal.evidence: Reviewer_iUkv edited its review on 2021-08-26 and wrote in the discussion: 'I increase my score from 5 to 6.' Reviewer_9UEy and Reviewer_kvzq never edited, so their 8 and 7 predate the rebuttal, and neither posted a reply.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: Point-by-point notation answers (order of set differences, the a/B shorthand, the meaning of observational, unconditional and nonmarginal) convinced Reviewer_iUkv that the problems are fixable in revision. iUkv still asked for a running example and clearer notation.

ac.evidence: Acceptance follows 8/6/7, but the oral tier goes beyond the reviews: the top score is 8 ('Top 50% of accepted NeurIPS papers'), no reviewer argued for an oral, and the meta-review's only praise is 'a solid and novel theoretical contribution'. Its point that the abstract should say the full joint distribution is not given is the AC's own.

main_reasons_for_decision: AC judged it 'a solid and novel theoretical contribution' and chose the oral tier without a reviewer asking for it
Reviewer support 8/7/6 at 6 to 7 hours each; Reviewer_kvzq (confidence 4) called it 'a very strong contribution' and a strict generalization
Readability problems treated as fixable; Reviewer_iUkv raised 5 to 6 after the notation answers

issues_only_a: Theorem 2's surrogate set reduces the problem to MGT; the contribution is not deep (Reviewer_h23K)
Better suited to a journal; proofs need days to check (Reviewer_6Pv4)
Citation style, missing references (Greenland & Lash 2008; Carroll et al. 2006) and a matrix-dimension typo (Reviewer_6Pv4); P_r clutter and an undefined admissible set (Reviewer_h23K)
issues_only_b: Rank condition of Miao et al.; assumptions 'strewn throughout and often made opaque' (Reviewer_kvzq)
Practical estimation of the identified formulas may be very hard (Reviewer_kvzq)
Too much space on the single- and double-proxy settings; no running example of the algorithm (Reviewer_iUkv)
A table relating ID-ME to recent identification algorithms (Reviewer_9UEy)
Abstract and introduction should say that the full joint distribution is not given (Committee B meta-review)
shared_issues: Dense, overloaded notation, including the slash notation of Lemma 2 (Reviewer_rBKj in A, Reviewer_iUkv in B)
Proofs not checked by most reviewers
Soundness without completeness (Reviewer_h23K and Reviewer_rBKj in A, Reviewer_9UEy in B)
No experiments: held against the paper in A (Reviewer_yA7o), explicitly not in B (Reviewer_kvzq)
Need for more intuition and examples; unclear definitions of distribution types near lines 80-82 (Reviewer_6Pv4 in A, Reviewer_iUkv in B)
verdict: Committee B recommended more because its reviewers rated the same facts higher, and its area chair chose an oral that no reviewer asked for. Neither committee found an error in a result; both found the notation dense, and most reviewers checked no proofs. Committee A's four reviewers, at confidence 2 or 3, each settled on 6. Reviewer_h23K's critique that Theorem 2 reruns the MGT loop with a surrogate experiment is accurate and went unanswered, but it did not push anyone below acceptance; A's area chair took the flat 6s and the reading difficulty as the verdict: poster. Committee B's reviewers spent 6 to 7 hours each; Reviewer_kvzq (confidence 4) called the paper 'a very strong contribution', Reviewer_9UEy gave 8, and the notation critic Reviewer_iUkv rose from 5 to 6 after the rebuttal. Still, a top score of 8 ('Top 50% of accepted NeurIPS papers') and no reviewer request do not make an oral; the oral tier is the B area chair's own call, justified in one generic sentence. The discrepancy is the reviewer pool plus area-chair discretion at the award tier, not different facts.
candidate_reasons: Readability weighed as limiting, not fixable
